rationale: The objective (communication_kernel_sum_ms, max-rank NCCL kernel duration sum, median of 3 profiled samples) is produced only by the 13 fp32 c10d::allreduce_ bucket invocations of DDP's final-micro-batch reducer: call d0938de87369efd500322679 (12 buckets of 7,087,872 elements) and call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b (the 39,385,344-element last bucket), 497,759,232 B of gradient payload per rank in total. Measured facts from the supplied records: the clean objective (63.32/63.67 ms on ranks 0/1) matches the warmed intrinsic back-to-back collective cost at exactly these sizes (collective_calibration: 12 x 3.536 ms + 19.383 ms), so the metric is transfer-bound, not overlap- or skew-bound; the executed kernel is ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL launched as grid [2,1,1] x block [544,1,1] on the no-P2P two-RTX-4090 PCIe4 topology, i.e. 2 channels; achieved logical throughput is ~8.0-8.1 GB/s per direction, consistent with the tuner's LL rating (8.6 GB/s) and about half of its RING Simple/LL128 ratings (19.8/19.0 GB/s). Bytes, dtypes, bucket layout (bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view, broadcast_buffers=False), no_sync accumulation, SGD and the default process group are frozen contract invariants, so bucket fusion, compression, hooks and DDP reconfiguration are excluded. This candidate is the selected joint hypothesis: both allreduce_ sites get a joint functional replacement that performs the identical fp32 SUM bucket allreduce (same tensor list reduced in place, same async semantics, same (Tensor[], Work) return through the real c10d::allreduce_ operator) on a lazily created, identically-membership NCCL process group whose communicator is initialized with raised channel parallelism (NCCL_NCHANNELS) and optionally a pinned protocol (NCCL_PROTO), with the expectation of raising per-kernel SHM ring throughput from ~8 GB/s toward the PCIe ceiling and cutting the kernel-duration sum roughly proportionally (target ~35-45 ms). This expectation is a hypothesis to be measured, not an observed capability; whether channel scaling raises SHM bus bandwidth and whether protocol pinning helps at 28 MB payloads are unknowns the parameter search resolves empirically (nchannels 0/4/8/16 x proto default/Simple/LL128; 0/default arms isolate channel-only, protocol-only and control effects). Numerics: a 2-rank ring/tree SUM reduces each element exactly once from the two replicas and broadcasts the identical bytes, so cross-rank gradients stay bit-identical (exact_gradient_replica_check at atol=0/rtol=0), and the serial-reference checks (1e-6/1e-4) see the same single-addition values as the baseline; parameters, gradients and the optimizer step are untouched. The tuned communicator is created once on the first replacement invocation (first quality/warmup step, per the binding contract's lazy-setup allowance) symmetrically on both ranks via dist.new_group(backend='nccl', device_id=<bucket device>), with env overrides applied only around creation/eager-init and restored after the first successful tuned call; the worker's default-group communicator (already initialized during prepare) and the gloo control group are untouched, and no other NCCL communicator is created in the worker afterwards, so env-based tuning stays confined to the new communicator. Fallbacks keep the parent semantics exactly: unsupported signature (defensive runtime guards beyond the framework signature match), setup failure (communicator creation error; permanent per-process fallback with a concise label) and runtime failure (tuned call raised; per-process fallback) all route the unmodified parent operator with the original arguments, so quality, state and alias semantics never depend on the tuned path. Clean step_ms is expected to be unchanged or better (the reduced kernels lie inside the timed step) and must stay within the 1.05x constraint; the rendezvous and communicator-init cost occur only in the first, un-timed quality invocation. No bundle is replaced or required (installed_bundles is empty); no inner call is eliminated - the 13 collectives still run, on the tuned communicator - so plan recapture and consumers (DDP finalize, optimizer.step on gradient-as-bucket-view buffers) remain valid. There is no inputs/previous-feedback.txt to address in this attempt. A CPU two-rank dress rehearsal of this exact file against the framework's own discovery/binding machinery (gloo backend substituted) confirmed: replacements installed for every observed allreduce_ site, lazy single group creation, all bucket calls routed through the tuned group, coverage counted, and loss/gradients/parameters bit-identical to the parent across repeated continuous steps, with the setup-failure path also producing bit-identical results through the parent.
setup_work: Lazy, once per worker process, inside the first replacement invocation (never at build time, never inside a timed or profiled window): (1) read nchannels/proto from context['parameters']; (2) set NCCL_NCHANNELS (only if nchannels > 0) and NCCL_PROTO (only if proto != 'default') in os.environ; (3) dist.new_group(backend='nccl', timeout=300s, device_id=<device of the first bucket tensor>) - identical membership (all ranks) and identical call point on both ranks, rendezvous is the only blocking cost; (4) box the ProcessGroup for the c10d operator and cache it in module state; (5) after the first successful tuned allreduce (or a runtime failure), restore the previous environment values, so the overrides are observable to no communicator other than the lazily initialized one. Build-time work is limited to building two closures; no model parameters are transformed, no fixture-dependent data is cached, and the workload executes on current inputs every invocation. Device-memory effect: the additional NCCL communicator allocates its channel/proxy buffers outside the PyTorch caching allocator (roughly a few MB per channel; e.g. ~16-64 MB at 4-16 channels plus fixed overhead), which is invisible to peak_allocated/reserved counters but is real driver memory; PyTorch-side setup allocation is negligible. The first (cold) quality invocation additionally pays communicator bootstrap (~seconds), which the warm-model timing and the 3 profiled samples never see.
quality_risks: If the tuned call raised at runtime on only one rank mid-collective, the peer could stall until the NCCL timeout; the code treats any tuned-call exception as a permanent per-process parent fallback, but an asymmetric hardware failure would still fail the step honestly rather than corrupt outputs.

Communicator creation inside the DDP reducer context is a rendezvous: both ranks must reach the first final-micro-bucket allreduce, which they do deterministically; the 300 s group timeout bounds the wait, well inside the 900 s worker timeout, and creation failure falls back to the parent on both ranks.

Protocol/channel changes could in principle alter reduction order; for 2-rank SUM each element is reduced exactly once and broadcast, so cross-rank replicas remain bit-identical and the serial-reference tolerances (1e-6/1e-4) are unaffected - verified bitwise on the CPU rehearsal with the framework's own binding path.

Defensive runtime guards (single fp32 CUDA bucket tensor, null sparse_indices, no extra args/kwargs) are stricter than the framework's signature match; any mismatch routes to the parent operator unchanged, which can only forfeit speed, not correctness.

The step_ms <= 1.05x baseline constraint relies on the communication lying inside the timed step; faster kernels reduce it, and no compute work is added on the warm path (one cached dict lookup, one counter, one op call).

The parameter arms nchannels=0 and proto='default' intentionally reproduce near-baseline communicator tuning; they exist as controls for attribution and must not be published as improvements if selected - the paired revalidation decides.
Extra NCCL channel buffers consume non-PyTorch device memory (see setup_work); at 24 GB per GPU and a ~2.5 GB workload this is not a constraint, but it is reported rather than hidden.

params.name: nchannels
params.description: NCCL_NCHANNELS forced on the lazily created tuned communicator only; 0 leaves NCCL's own channel choice (observed default 2 on this no-P2P topology) as a control arm.

params.name: proto
params.description: NCCL_PROTO pinned on the tuned communicator only; 'default' leaves the tuner's protocol choice as a control arm.
